content_units: A 90-minute kickoff can cover all required topics if the time-boxing is tight and decisions are captured live. The attendee with only 45 minutes of availability should be included in introductions, scope, and early risk input before leaving.
14:00-14:10 UTC   Open and align   Welcome; quick intros; confirm roles; restate outcomes   Shared understanding of who is in the room
14:10-14:25 UTC   Confirm project scope   Review goals; in-scope/out-of-scope; success criteria   Scope alignment and no major ambiguity
14:25-14:40 UTC   Surface early risks   Ask for blockers; dependencies; resourcing or timeline concerns   Initial risk list with owner candidates
14:40-14:45 UTC   Capture early input from partial attendee   Final comments from attendee leaving at 14:45; confirm any dependencies they own   Their input recorded before departure
14:45-15:05 UTC   Review milestones   Walk through phases; dates; decision gates; key handoffs   Draft milestone map and checkpoints
15:05-15:20 UTC   Define action items   Assign owners; due dates; communication cadence   Action register with clear next steps
15:20-15:30 UTC   Wrap and confirm   Recap decisions; confirm notes; validate next meeting timing   Agreed summary and follow-up plan
- Place their must-have contribution in the first 45 minutes.
- Ask them specifically for scope concerns, risks, and dependencies before 14:45 UTC.
- End exactly at 15:30 UTC so attendees have a full 10-minute buffer before any 15:40 UTC or later meeting.
- Avoid overruns; park unresolved items instead of extending.
- Use one shared notes doc visible to all.
- Nominate one facilitator and one note-taker.
- Timebox each section and announce “2 minutes left” warnings.
- Capture action items in the format: owner + task + due date.
- Keep introductions short: name, role, and what success looks like.
- Introductions: “What do you own, and what do you need from this project?”
- Scope: “What is definitely in, definitely out, and what still needs confirmation?”
- Risks: “What could delay delivery, reduce quality, or create dependency issues?”
- Milestones: “Which checkpoints require approval, input, or handoff?”
- Action items: “Who does what by when?”

Join us for the remote project kickoff to align on team roles, project scope, milestone plan, key risks, and immediate next steps. We will keep the session tightly time-boxed so we finish on time, capture decisions live, and leave everyone with clear action items and owners.

Using the provided time window, all three time zones fall within standard working hours, and the meeting ends with the required 10-minute buffer before a hypothetical next meeting at 15:40 UTC or later. The agenda is ordered to protect critical input from the attendee who can only stay for the first 45 minutes.
